excerptEn: Poly-B pipes fail silently in thousands of Vancouver homes. This guide covers what they are, why insurers are dropping coverage, and what a 2026 replacement costs — with real PEX upgrade timelines.
excerptZh: Poly-B 管道在大温数千套房屋中悄然失效。本文涵盖：它是什么、为何保险公司拒绝续保、2026 年更换费用实价——含 PEX 升级真实工期。
contentEn:
Does Your Vancouver Home Have Failing Poly-B Pipes?

If your home was built between 1985 and 1997 in Metro Vancouver, there is a roughly 40–60% chance it has Poly-B (polybutylene) plumbing — and a near-certainty that your home insurance provider knows it. Poly-B is a grey or dull-white plastic pipe, typically stamped "PB2110" or "Shell Oil" along its length, running from the main shutoff to every tap, toilet, shower, and appliance in the house. The chlorine in BC's water reacts with the pipe walls over two decades, causing brittleness, micro-cracks, and eventually catastrophic leaks. In 2026, multiple BC insurers will not renew home insurance on Poly-B properties at renewal — replacement is now a transactional necessity, not a maintenance preference. Reno Stars has replaced Poly-B plumbing in homes across Richmond, Vancouver, Burnaby, Surrey, and Coquitlam.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

How to Tell If Your Home Has Poly-B Pipes

Poly-B identification is straightforward for a licensed plumber and takes less than 30 minutes during a walkthrough. Look for these diagnostic markers:

  • Colour and texture: Grey or dull-white plastic, not bright white like modern PEX or copper-coloured like copper
  • Stamped markings: "PB2110," "PB1320," or "Shell Oil" printed along the pipe length every few feet
  • Location: Typically enters the home at the main shutoff valve, runs to a central manifold, then branches to each fixture
  • Era of home: If the home was built or significantly plumbed between 1985 and 1997 in Metro Vancouver, assume Poly-B until confirmed otherwise

The failure mode is progressive: pipes do not burst suddenly. Micro-cracks develop over years, reducing water pressure and creating pinhole leaks that go unnoticed until drywall damage appears. By the time a homeowner notices staining or musty smells, the internal pipe degradation is already extensive. Reno Stars includes a free Poly-B identification walkthrough with every renovation quote.

Why BC Insurers Are Dropping Poly-B Homes in 2026

The insurance crisis is the single biggest driver of Poly-B replacement decisions in 2026. Actuarial data from the Insurance Bureau of Canada shows that Poly-B homes have claim rates 3–5 times higher than homes with modern PEX or copper plumbing. The BC Financial Services Regulatory Authority (BCFSA) has not mandated insurers to drop Poly-B coverage, but several major residential carriers — including Aviva Canada, Sonnet, and Onlia — have updated their underwriting guidelines to exclude or surcharge homes with confirmed Poly-B plumbing.

The practical consequence: at your next home insurance renewal, your provider may demand a certified Poly-B replacement as a condition of renewal, or decline to renew at standard terms. Once one insurer has flagged the property, others in the market follow. This is why homeowners who discovered Poly-B during pre-purchase inspections in 2024 and 2025 are now being forced into emergency replacements at the worst possible time — with a purchase closing date looming and no negotiating leverage with contractors.

Poly-B replacement is not a home improvement. It is insurance maintenance. The cost of replacement ($4,000–$35,000) is almost always less than the deductible plus increased premiums on a non-renewed policy, plus the cost of repairing water damage from a failed pipe before replacement can happen.

What Poly-B Replacement Involves: PEX-A vs PEX-B

Reno Stars replaces Poly-B with PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) — the current Canadian Plumbing Code standard for residential supply piping. Two grades are used:

  • PEX-A (Uponor AquaPEX, Rehau Raupex): The premium grade. More flexible, more freeze-resistant, fewer fittings required because it bends around corners. Typical manufacturer warranty: 25-year limited, transferable to subsequent owners.
  • PEX-B (Cash Acme, Apollo): The standard grade. Slightly more fittings required because it is less flexible. Approved for use in all BC municipalities. Typical manufacturer warranty: 25-year limited.

For most Metro Vancouver homes, PEX-B provides equivalent long-term reliability at a lower material cost. PEX-A is recommended for homes in unheated crawl spaces or with freeze risk, and for homeowners who want the longest possible transferable warranty.

The replacement process:

  1. Isolate and drain the existing Poly-B system
  2. Access pipe runs through drywall (we use precision cutting to minimize wall damage)
  3. Remove all Poly-B from manifold to every fixture
  4. Install new PEX manifold and run new supply lines to each fixture
  5. Install new shutoff valves at each fixture
  6. Pressure-test the new system to code (typically 1.5x working pressure, held for 30 minutes)
  7. Patch and repair drywall access points
  8. BC building permit inspection and sign-off

Drain and waste (DWV) piping — the vertical soil stacks and drain lines — is not replaced during a standard Poly-B supply-line replacement. If your home has cast-iron DWV stacks showing corrosion or sags, that is a separate plumbing scope addressed outside the Poly-B replacement budget.

Poly-B Replacement Costs in Vancouver: 2026 Real Numbers

Poly-B replacement costs in 2026 reflect current BC trade rates, PEX material costs, and permit fees. All figures include: PEX-A or PEX-B re-pipe, all supply line connections, manifold installation, new shutoff valves, drywall access patching, pressure test, BC building permit and inspection. They do not include: drain/waste re-piping, hot water tank replacement, fixture upgrades, or full repainting of touched walls.

Condo, 1 bathroom, single floor$4,000 – $8,0002–3 days
Condo, 2 bathrooms$6,000 – $12,0003–4 days
Townhouse, 2 floors$8,000 – $14,0004–6 days
Single-family home, single floor, ~1,500 sqft$10,000 – $16,0005–7 days
Single-family home, 2 floors, ~2,500 sqft$14,000 – $22,0006–10 days
Luxury single-family home, 3 floors, multiple ensuites$20,000 – $35,000+10–14 days

Cost drivers above the typical range: knob-and-tube electrical wiring requiring rewire before plumbing access (add $10,000–$25,000); active water damage or mold requiring remediation (add $5,000–$20,000); copper drain lines requiring replacement as a连带 scope (add $3,000–$8,000).

Reno Stars provides fixed-price quotes after a 90-minute in-home walkthrough. Quotes are valid for 30 days and include all permit fees.

Poly-B in Strata Buildings: What Condo and Townhouse Owners Need to Know

Individual unit Poly-B replacement is complicated by shared plumbing infrastructure. In most Metro Vancouver condo and townhouse complexes built 1985–1997, the main supply risers (the vertical pipes serving multiple units) are typically owned by the strata corporation — not individual unit owners. If the building's risers are Poly-B, an individual unit replacement may not satisfy insurer requirements if the common-area supply lines remain Poly-B.

Reno Stars works directly with strata councils and property managers on building-wide Poly-B replacement projects. Coordinated building-wide replacement reduces per-unit cost by 15–25% versus individual unit work because mobilization, permit, and inspection costs are shared. Several Metro Vancouver stratas in Richmond, Surrey, and Burnaby have passed special levies for this purpose in 2025 and 2026. If your building has not yet addressed Poly-B, contact your strata property manager to schedule an engineering assessment. Individual unit owners can proceed with supply-line replacement inside their unit while coordinating with the strata on the common-area riser timeline.

How Long Does Poly-B Replacement Take?

The physical installation time varies by property size. However, the total project timeline includes a permit approval period that typically adds 1–3 weeks before work can begin. Current BC building permit processing times in Metro Vancouver average 10–15 business days for plumbing permits. Reno Stars pulls the permit and schedules inspection as part of every replacement contract.

For a typical Richmond condo with 1 bathroom, the on-site work is complete in 2 days. The home is habitable throughout — residents can stay in the unit but should expect to be without water for approximately 4–6 hours on the primary plumbing day while connections are transferred.

Does Home Insurance Cost Go Down After Poly-B Replacement?

Most BC insurers reduce premiums or re-qualify previously declined renewals after certified Poly-B replacement. The key document is a completion certificate from a licensed plumber confirming the replacement and a passing pressure test result. Reno Stars provides both at project close. Several clients in Richmond and North Vancouver have reported insurance premium reductions of $800–$1,500 per year following replacement, based on insurer re-underwriting the property as a modern plumbing risk class. The amortization of a $10,000–$14,000 replacement at $1,000/year in premium savings is 10–14 years — shorter if the alternative was a forced non-renewal or a higher-risk-surcharge policy.

How do I know if my Vancouver home has Poly-B pipes?

Look for grey or dull-white plastic pipe stamped "PB2110" or "Shell Oil" running from your main shutoff to fixtures. If your home was built between 1985 and 1997 in Metro Vancouver, assume Poly-B is present until confirmed otherwise by a licensed plumber. Reno Stars performs free Poly-B identification walkthroughs as part of our quote process.

Will my home insurance go up if I have Poly-B pipes?

Multiple BC insurers have updated underwriting guidelines to exclude or surcharge homes with confirmed Poly-B plumbing. The practical risk is non-renewal at your next policy anniversary, not just a premium increase. Replacing Poly-B with certified PEX piping typically restores eligibility for standard coverage and may reduce premiums — several Richmond and North Vancouver clients have reported $800–$1,500/year in premium savings after replacement.

How long does Poly-B replacement take in a Vancouver condo?

A single-level, 1-bathroom condo takes 2–3 days on site. You will need to be out of the unit for the primary plumbing day (approximately 4–6 hours without water). Add 1–3 weeks for BC building permit approval before work begins. Total project timeline from quote to completion: approximately 4–6 weeks.

Can I stay in my home during Poly-B replacement?

Yes, for most residential projects. The water is shut off for approximately 4–6 hours on the primary plumbing day, but running water is restored each evening. For multi-floor single-family homes where both bathrooms share a manifold location, you may need to plan around brief water outages on 2 consecutive days.

What is the difference between PEX-A and PEX-B for Poly-B replacement?

PEX-A (premium grade) is more flexible and freeze-resistant, requiring fewer fittings. PEX-B (standard grade) is code-approved in all BC municipalities and provides equivalent long-term reliability at a lower material cost. Reno Stars recommends PEX-A for homes in unheated crawl spaces or for owners seeking the longest transferable warranty. Both carry 25-year manufacturer warranties.

您的温哥华房屋是否有即将失效的 Poly-B 管道？

如果您的房屋于 1985 年至 1997 年间建於大温哥华地区，有 40% 至 60% 的概率装有 Poly-B（聚丁烯）水管——而且您的房屋保险公司几乎肯定知情。Poly-B 是一种灰色或暗白色塑料管，通常沿管道每隔几英尺印有「PB2110」或「Shell Oil」标识，从主截流阀一直延伸到房屋每个水龙头、马桶、淋浴设备和电器。卑诗省自来水中所含的氯与管道壁发生化学反应，历经二十多年，导致管道变脆、产生微裂纹，最终发生严重漏水。进入 2026 年，多家卑诗省保险公司已更新承保准则，不再为确认装有 Poly-B 的物业续保——更换不再只是维护选项，而是交易必要条件。聚星装修已在列治文、温哥华、本拿比、素里和高贵林的房屋中完成了 Poly-B 管道更换。

正在计划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？获取聚星装修的免费、无义务报价。

如何判断您的房屋是否有 Poly-B 管道

Poly-B 识别对持牌水管工来说很简单，勘察时间不超过 30 分钟。查找以下诊断标志：

  • 颜色和质地：灰色或暗白色塑料，不像现代 PEX 那样亮白，也不像铜管那样呈铜色
  • 压印标识：沿管道每间隔几英尺印有「PB2110」、「PB1320」或「Shell Oil」
  • 位置：通常从主截流阀进入房屋，连接到中央分水器，再分支到各用水设备
  • 房屋建造年代：如果房屋于 1985 年至 1997 年间在大温哥华地区建或进行过大规模管道工程，在持牌水管工确认之前，请先假定存在 Poly-B

失效模式是渐进式的：管道不会突然爆裂。微裂纹历经多年发展，水压逐渐降低，并产生不被察觉的针眼漏水，直到墙面出现水渍或霉味。此时，管道内部降解已相当严重。聚星装修在每次装修报价中均包含免费 Poly-B 识别勘察。

为何卑诗省保险公司在 2026 年拒绝为 Poly-B 房屋续保

保险危机是 2026 年 Poly-B 更换决策的最大单一驱动因素。加拿大保险局（Insurance Bureau of Canada）的精算数据显示，Poly-B 房屋的索赔率比装有现代 PEX 或铜管的房屋高 3 至 5 倍。卑诗省金融服务监管局（BCFSA）尚未强制要求保险公司拒保 Poly-B 房屋，但包括 Aviva Canada、Sonnet 和 Onlia 在内的多家主要住宅保险公司已更新承保准则，对确认装有 Poly-B 水管的房屋拒保或附加 surcharge。

实际后果：在您的下一次房屋保险续保时，您的供应商可能要求提供认证的 Poly-B 更换作为续保条件，或拒绝按标准条款续保。一旦一家保险公司标记了该物业，市场上其他公司就会跟进。这就是为什么在 2024 年和 2025 年购房检查期间发现 Poly-B 的房主现在被迫在最糟糕的时机进行紧急更换——购买交割日期迫在眉睫，与承包商议价的能力为零。

Poly-B 更换不是房屋改善工程。它是保险维护工作。更换费用（$4,000–$35,000）几乎总是低于未续保后的自付额加上上涨的保费，再加上更换前发生故障管道维修费用。

Poly-B 更换涉及什么：PEX-A 与 PEX-B

聚星装修用 PEX（交联聚乙烯）替换 Poly-B——这是加拿大水管规范 residential supply piping 的现行标准。使用两种等级：

  • PEX-A（Uponor AquaPEX、Rehau Raupex）：高级等级。更柔软，更耐低温，需要的接头更少，因为在拐角处弯曲。典型厂家保修期：25 年有限期，可转让给后续业主。
  • PEX-B（Cash Acme、Apollo）：标准等级。因为柔软度较低，需要更多接头。在所有卑诗省市政均已获批准使用。典型厂家保修期：25 年有限期。

对于大多数大温哥华住宅，PEX-B 以更低的材料成本提供同等的长期可靠性。PEX-A 推荐用于无暖气 crawl spaces 或有冻融风险的房屋，以及希望获得最长可转让保修期的业主。

更换流程：

  1. 隔离并排空现有 Poly-B 系统
  2. 通过干墙进行管道检修（我们使用精确切割以最大限度减少墙面损坏）
  3. 从分水器到每个设备拆除所有 Poly-B
  4. 安装新 PEX 分水器并为每个设备铺设新的供水管路
  5. 为每个设备安装新的截流阀
  6. 对新系统进行规范压力测试（通常为工作压力的 1.5 倍，保持 30 分钟）
  7. 修补并修复干墙检修口
  8. 卑诗省建筑许可证检验和签收

排水和废物（DWV）管道——垂直粪管和排水管线——在标准 Poly-B 供水管线更换期间不更换。如果您的房屋排水管显示出腐蚀或凹陷，那是单独的管道工程范围，不在 Poly-B 更换预算内。

温哥华 Poly-B 更换费用：2026 年真实数字

2026 年 Poly-B 更换费用反映当前卑诗省工艺费率、PEX 材料成本和许可费用。所有数字包含：PEX-A 或 PEX-B 重新走管、所有供水接头、分水器安装、新截流阀、干墙检修口修补、压力测试、卑诗省建筑许可证和检验。不含：排水/废物改管、热水器更换、洁具升级或受影响墙面的全面重新粉刷。

物业类型更换费用（2026 年）典型工期
公寓，1 间浴室，单层$4,000 – $8,0002–3 天
公寓，2 间浴室$6,000 – $12,0003–4 天
联排别墅，2 层$8,000 – $14,0004–6 天
独立屋，单层，约 1,500 平尺$10,000 – $16,0005–7 天
独立屋，2 层，约 2,500 平尺$14,000 – $22,0006–10 天
豪华独立屋，3 层，多间主卫套房$20,000 – $35,000+10–14 天

超出典型范围的成本驱动因素：更换前需要重新布线的旋钮和管式电线（增加 $10,000–$25,000）；需要 remediation 的活动性漏水或霉菌（增加 $5,000–$20,000）；需要更换的铜排水管线作为连带工程（增加 $3,000–$8,000）。

聚星装修在 90 分钟上门勘察后提供固定价格报价。报价有效期为 30 天，包含所有许可证费用。

公寓楼宇中的 Poly-B：共管物业业主须知

独立单元 Poly-B 更换因共享管道基础设施而复杂化。在大多数 1985–1997 年间建造的大温哥华公寓和联排别墅小区，主要供水立管（服务多个单元的垂直管道）通常归业主委员会所有——而非个别单元业主。如果楼栋的立管是 Poly-B，单个单元更换可能无法满足保险公司的承保要求（如果公共区域供水管线仍然是 Poly-B）。

聚星装修直接与业主委员会和物业管理公司合作，进行楼栋统一 Poly-B 更换工程。统筹楼栋统一更换与单独单元工程相比，每个单元成本降低 15% 至 25%，因为动员、许可证和检验费用可以分摊。列治文、素里和本拿比的几个业主委员会已在 2025 年和 2026 年通过了特别征收费用用于此目的。如果您的楼栋尚未处理 Poly-B，请联系您的业主委员会物业管理公司安排工程评估。独立单元业主可以在与业主委员会协调公共区域立管工期的同时，先对单元内供水管线进行更换。

Poly-B 更换需要多长时间？

实际安装时间因物业规模而异。但是，总项目时间包括许可批准期，这通常在工作开始前增加 1–3 周。大温哥华地区目前卑诗省建筑许可处理时间平均为 10–15 个工作日。聚星装修作为每个更换合同的一部分办理许可证并安排检验。

对于典型的列治文 1 浴室公寓，现场工作可在 2 天内完成。房屋在整个过程中可正常居住——居民可留在单元内，但主要管道施工日预计停水约 4–6 小时。

Poly-B 更换后房屋保险费用会降低吗？

大多数卑诗省保险公司在认证的 Poly-B 更换完成后降低保费或重新批准先前拒保的续保。关键文件是持牌水管工的完工证书（确认更换）和压力测试通过结果。聚星装修在项目结束时提供这两份文件。列治文和北温哥华的几位客户报告，更换后保险 premiums 减少了 $800–$1,500/年，基于保险公司将物业重新 underwrite 为现代管道风险类别。以每年 $1,000 的保费 savings 计算，$10,000–$14,000 更换的摊销期为 10–14 年——如果替代方案是被迫 non-renewal 或更高风险附加费政策，则更短。

正在计划厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？获取聚星装修的免费、无义务报价。

如何判断我的温哥华房屋是否有 Poly-B 管道？

查找从主截流阀延伸到用水设备的灰色或暗白色塑料管，上面印有「PB2110」或「Shell Oil」。如果您的房屋于 1985 年至 1997 年间建於大温哥华地区，在持牌水管工确认之前，请先假定存在 Poly-B。聚星装修在报价过程中免费提供 Poly-B 识别勘察。

装有 Poly-B 管道会影响我的房屋保险吗？

多家卑诗省保险公司已更新承保准则，对确认装有 Poly-B 水管的房屋拒保或附加附加费。实际风险是在下次保单周年时保险人拒绝续保，而不仅仅是保费上涨。在认证的 PEX 管道更换后，通常可恢复标准承保资格，保费也可能降低——列治文和北温哥华的多位客户在更换后报告每年保费节省 $800–$1,500。

温哥华公寓 Poly-B 更换需要多长时间？

单层 1 浴室公寓现场工作需要 2–3 天。您需要在主管道施工日离开单元（约 4–6 小时无水）。工作开始前需增加 1–3 周的卑诗省建筑许可审批时间。从报价到完工的整个项目时间：约 4–6 周。

Poly-B 更换期间我可以住在家里吗？

可以，对于大多数住宅项目。水在主要管道施工日关闭约 4–6 小时，但每天晚上都会恢复供水。对于多层独立屋（两个浴室共用一个分水器位置），您可能需要计划连续 2 天短暂停水。

PEX-A 和 PEX-B 在 Poly-B 更换中有什么区别？

PEX-A（高级等级）更柔软、更耐低温，需要的接头更少。PEX-B（标准等级）在所有卑诗省市政均已获批准使用，提供同等长期可靠性且材料成本更低。聚星装修推荐将 PEX-A 用于无暖气 crawl spaces 或希望获得最长可转让保修期的业主。两者均享有 25 年厂家保修。
